pairing them separates observed field contact from the respondent's sponsorship belief, since an approach by representatives need not mean the respondent names a party as sender, and losing Q97 would leave the approach with no counterpart attribution."},{"challenges":[],"evidence":[{"field":"Q106D","quote":"Did you feel threatened during the interview?"},{"field":"Q106E","quote":"Were you physically threatened during the interview?"}],"id":"RQ106DE","items":["Q106D","Q106E"],"kind":"ADD","text":"Q106E narrows the felt-threat item Q106D to bodily threat, so a felt danger can be reported without a physical threat; dropping Q106E would conceal that distinction and make the two-word difference between them unreadable."},{"challenges":[],"evidence":[{"field":"Q109F","quote":"honest, in between, or misleading?"}],"id":"RQ109F","items":["Q109F"],"kind":"ADD","text":"Q109F is a three-point interviewer judgment of respondent candor during the encounter, an attributed demeanour rather than a verified check of answer accuracy or a respondent self-report."},{"challenges":[],"evidence":[{"field":"Q28","quote":"must always obey the laws and the courts"},{"field":"Q29B","quote":"never intervene in the country's political process"}],"id":"RQ2829B","items":["Q28","Q29B"],"kind":"ADD","text":"Q28 asks whether the president is bound by law and courts while Q29B asks whether the armed forces may take control when leaders abuse power; the shared wording makes the office the varying element, and without Q48B the MP answer could not be placed against the presidential counterpart."},{"challenges":[],"evidence":[{"field":"Q50B","quote":"she will be criticized, called names, or harassed"},{"field":"Q51A","quote":"should government and elected officials be doing more"}],"id":"RQ50B51A","items":["Q50B","Q51A"],"kind":"ADD","text":"Q50B is an anticipated community reaction to a hypothetical woman candidate, while Q51A is a demand about government effort on women's rights; the first describes expected social sanction and the second a desired state action, so consent to more government action need not imply belief that harassment is likely, and dropping Q50B would leave the demand without its social-condition counterpart."},{"challenges":[],"evidence":[{"field":"Q51B","quote":"which of the following issues related to women's rights and equality"}],"id":"RQ51B","items":["Q51B"],"kind":"ADD","text":"Q51B forces a single most-important choice among an offered women's-rights list, so it yields a capped priority ranking that is not independent salience for each listed issue;
